2609.20989.title: Trustworthy FinAInce: Unpacking How AI-Mediated Financial Advice is Judged
2609.20989.paper_summary: As generative AI is increasingly used as a source of personal financial guidance, understanding how people appraise such advice is important for supporting appropriate reliance. We conducted a randomized vignette experiment with 285 U.S. adults across eight financial decisions, independently varying three advice styles---AI, expert, and online community---and displayed source labels while holding the underlying recommendation consistent. Advice style most strongly shaped message and safety appraisals, Expert labels selectively increased perceived source knowledge, and decision context primarily shaped risk and safety appraisals. These appraisals were associated with downstream judgments, with models explaining 69.2% of overall quality, 75.9% of trust, and 82.9% of intended reliance. Expert-style advice also remained most preferred when shown without source labels. Our findings have implications for understanding financial advice evaluation, distinguishing the roles of advice style and source labels, and designing financial AI that supports grounded evaluation rather than simply maximizing trust.
2609.20989.paper_summary_zh: 隨著生成式人工智慧越來越多地被用作個人財務指導的來源，了解人們如何評價這些建議對於支持適當的依賴至關重要。<lb/>我們對285名美國成年人進行了一項隨機小品實驗，涵蓋八個財務決策，獨立變化三種建議風格——AI、專家和在線社區——並在保持基本建議一致的同時顯示來源標籤。<lb/>建議風格最強烈地影響了信息和安全評估，專家標籤選擇性地提高了感知的來源知識，而決策背景主要影響風險和安全評估。<lb/>這些評估與後續判斷相關，模型解釋了69.2%的整體質量、75.9%的信任和82.9%的預期依賴。<lb/>專家風格的建議在未顯示來源標籤的情況下仍然是最受偏好的。<lb/>我們的研究結果對理解財務建議評估、區分建議風格和來源標籤的角色，以及設計支持基於事實的評估而非僅僅是最大化信任的財務AI具有重要意義。
